requirements.requirement: Keep node1's installed curl package at its existing version when the system is updated.
requirements.summary: curl began at 8.17.0-r1 and was constrained in APK's world file to that exact version. With repository version 8.22.0-r0 available, an APK system-upgrade simulation planned 58 other upgrades but no curl upgrade; the installed version and constraint also persisted across reboot.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied. Direct evidence shows curl pinned to its original 8.17.0-r1 version and excluded from a simulated system upgrade despite 8.22.0-r0 being available. The provider restart protocol was also complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed interruption, changed boot identity, recovered services, and persistence of the curl hold. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The upgrade was simulated rather than applied, and APK warned that the simulation might be unreliable because a preupgrade was available. The exact world constraint and repeated simulation nevertheless provide strong supporting evidence.

The lifecycle collector cannot assess failed OpenRC services through its systemd-specific failed-service probe; executor rc-status output directly showed expected services started before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The index refresh supported upgrade evaluation, the exact-version APK operation implemented the required hold, and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated system mutation was observed. The only unwanted residue was /tmp/node-reboot.log, created by the restart command and retained after completion; it was low-risk but not cleaned up.
